req.title: Sequence header order preservation
req.statement: The system shall preserve the client-supplied order of duplicate headers in the /headers echo response.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that the /headers endpoint must preserve the client-supplied order of duplicate headers in the echo response. The key challenge is that HTTP/1.1 allows multiple headers with the same name, and the server must echo them in the original order. We test: (1) positive case with two distinct custom headers echoed correctly, (2) negative case verifying that a missing header is not present in the response, (3) boundary case with a single duplicate header name sent twice to verify order preservation. We also test the exact HTTP 200 status code and the exact JSON structure. Note: Flask's test client merges duplicate headers into a comma-separated string per WSGI spec (PEP 3333), so we assert on the comma-joined value and its order. We design assertions to catch mutations on status codes, key presence, and value ordering.

tests.name: test_headers_positive_two_distinct_custom_headers_echoed
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with two distinct custom headers X-First and X-Second
Parse JSON response body
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: system shall preserve client-supplied headers in /headers echo response
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_positive_two_distinct_custom_headers_echoed():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={
        'X-First': 'alpha',
        'X-Second': 'beta'
    })
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-First' in hdrs
    assert 'X-Second' in hdrs
    assert hdrs['X-First'] == 'alpha'
    assert hdrs['X-Second'] == 'beta'

test_headers_positive_two_distinct_custom_headers_echoed()

tests.name: test_headers_boundary_single_duplicate_header_order_preserved
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
WSGI merges duplicate header names into comma-separated string
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with X-Order header appearing twice: first 'first', then 'second'
Parse JSON response body
Check that the echoed value contains both values with 'first' before 'second'
expected: Index of 'first' in the value string is less than index of 'second'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: duplicate header order must be preserved — first value before second value
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_boundary_single_duplicate_header_order_preserved():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers=[
        ('X-Order', 'first'),
        ('X-Order', 'second')
    ])
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Order' in hdrs
    val = hdrs['X-Order']
    assert 'first' in val
    assert 'second' in val
    assert val.index('first') < val.index('second')

test_headers_boundary_single_duplicate_header_order_preserved()

tests.name: test_headers_positive_exact_status_200_and_json_structure
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with a known custom header
Assert exact status code 200
Assert top-level JSON key is exactly 'headers'
Assert the custom header value is exactly correct
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200 (not 201, not 204)
JSON body has exactly the key 'headers' at top level
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: HTTP 2xx response with expected payload; exact 200 for GET /headers
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_positive_exact_status_200_and_json_structure():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Trace-Id': 'trace-42'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 204
    data = r.get_json()
    assert list(data.keys()) == ['headers']
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert hdrs['X-Trace-Id'] == 'trace-42'
    assert hdrs['X-Trace-Id'] != 'trace-43'

test_headers_positive_exact_status_200_and_json_structure()

tests.name: test_headers_boundary_three_duplicate_headers_order_preserved
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
WSGI merges duplicate header names into comma-separated string
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with X-Seq header three times: 'a', 'b', 'c'
Parse JSON response body
Verify all three values present and in order a < b < c by index
expected: Position of 'a' < position of 'b' < position of 'c' in the echoed string
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: three duplicate headers — order of all three must be preserved
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_boundary_three_duplicate_headers_order_preserved():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers=[
        ('X-Seq', 'a'),
        ('X-Seq', 'b'),
        ('X-Seq', 'c')
    ])
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Seq' in hdrs
    val = hdrs['X-Seq']
    assert 'a' in val
    assert 'b' in val
    assert 'c' in val
    assert val.index('a') < val.index('b')
    assert val.index('b') < val.index('c')

test_headers_boundary_three_duplicate_headers_order_preserved()

tests.name: test_headers_negative_wrong_method_post_returns_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send POST /headers (wrong HTTP method)
Assert status code is 405 Method Not Allowed
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: error pathway — HTTP 4xx on client error (wrong method)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_negative_wrong_method_post_returns_405():
    r = client.post('/headers', headers={'X-Custom': 'value'})
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 500

test_headers_negative_wrong_method_post_returns_405()

tests.name: test_headers_positive_header_value_exact_not_partial
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with X-Exact-Val: 'hello-world'
Assert echoed value is exactly 'hello-world', not a substring or superset
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: exact value preservation — not truncated, not augmented
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_positive_header_value_exact_not_partial():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Exact-Val': 'hello-world'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Exact-Val' in hdrs
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Val'] == 'hello-world'
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Val'] != 'hello'
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Val'] != 'world'
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Val'] != 'hello-world-extra'

test_headers_positive_header_value_exact_not_partial()
